text: Name a mixture-of-experts model or routing method
note: Sparse MoE models (past and present) and the routers, balancing tricks and training methods behind them

answers.q: Skip the learned router: hash each token's ID to pick its expert. Competitive with Switch. Rude.
Over a million tiny experts, picked by product-key retrieval.
Treat routing as a linear assignment problem so every expert gets an equal share.
Route tokens around whole blocks instead of between experts. Compute only where it matters.
Block-sparse kernels so no token ever gets dropped. Dropless MoE.
Copy a dense checkpoint's FFN into every expert and keep training.
How many tokens each expert may take. Overflow tokens get dropped and skip the layer.
ST-MoE's penalty on large router logits. Keeps training from blowing up.
DeepSeek-V3 nudges per-expert bias terms instead of adding a balancing loss.
AI21's sandwich of Transformer, Mamba and MoE layers.
A dense transformer plus a 128-expert residual MoE. 480B parameters in total.
Its tech report confirmed a sparse MoE under the million-token context.
Jacobs, Jordan, Nowlan & Hinton, 1991. Where it all started.
1.2T parameters, trained with about a third of GPT-3's energy.
Shazeer et al. 2017, 'Outrageously Large Neural Networks': a 137B-parameter MoE between LSTM layers.
Many small, fine-grained experts plus always-on shared experts.
xAI's 314B open-weights MoE, 2 of 8 experts per token.
Databricks: 16 experts, 4 per token, for 65x more expert combinations than Mixtral.
Meta's first MoE Llamas: Scout and Maverick.
OpenAI's open-weight MoEs (120b and 20b), shipped in MXFP4.
Moonshot's 1T-parameter MoE with 32B active, trained with the MuonClip optimizer.
Add tunable Gaussian noise before the top-k so the experts share the load.
No discrete routing: each expert slot gets a weighted blend of all the tokens.
Google's 2020 600B-parameter MoE translator, sharded across 2048 TPU cores by annotation.
Flip it: experts pick their top-k tokens, so load balance is perfect by construction.
'8x7B' with top-2 routing, yet ~47B total, since only the FFNs are multiplied.
Route each token to exactly one expert. The simplest router, scaled to 1.6T parameters.
671B total, 37B active, aux-loss-free balancing, and a reported ~$5.6M of final-run GPU time.
